name: Tunar Ahmadzada
tagline: 11th-grade researcher working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and computational mathematics
summary: 11th-grade student pursuing independent work at the intersection of artificial intelligence and computational mathematics. Selected as one of four students nationwide to represent Azerbaijan at the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (IOAI), earning a Gold Medal at the National Round. Research in algorithmic number theory received national recognition at ISEF, while an applied computational project received NASA's Galactic Problem Solver award. Seeking to build on this research-driven foundation through rigorous undergraduate study in Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence.

projects.title: NeuroQuit: An EEG-Based Wearable for Early Nicotine Craving Detection
projects.tag: Team project — The Junior Academy, The New York Academy of Sciences
projects.description: Proposed a non-invasive, ear-worn EEG wearable that uses AI to detect early nicotine craving before smoking occurs, addressing the gap that most cessation methods intervene only after a person has decided to smoke. Designed a multimodal approach: per-user calibration on baseline and controlled-craving EEG data, machine-learning analysis of alpha and theta activity, and fusion with heart rate and galvanic skin response to reduce false alerts. Concept includes real-time voice prompts and daily craving reports for users and clinicians, with evaluation planned on detection accuracy, precision, recall, and false-alert rate; positioned as an assistive intervention, not a cure.

projects.title: Common Divisibility Framework for Prime Numbers
projects.description: Researched divisibility properties of prime numbers and developed a single generalized algorithm capable of determining divisibility by any positive integer, unifying classical divisor-specific rules into one method. Presented at Azerbaijan's national ISEF qualifying round, earning a Bronze Medal in Mathematics against republic-level candidates.

projects.title: Space Debris Recycling System
projects.tag: NASA Space Apps Challenge — Global Hackathon
projects.description: Designed a device concept for the efficient, sustainable management of space debris, enabling in-orbit debris to be repurposed as raw material and 3D-printed on-site into spare parts needed for spacecraft and station maintenance. Built the computational solution within a 48-hour international hackathon, applying data analysis and rapid-prototyping methods to model the debris-to-part production workflow. Awarded the "Galactic Problem Solver" distinction.

experience.org: The Junior Academy — The New York Academy of Sciences
points: Selected for an application-based program that places high school students from around the world into international teams guided by STEM mentors, with the aim of preparing the next generation of innovators.
Collaborate across countries in 10-week virtual Innovation Challenges: researching, designing, testing, and pitching solutions to real-world problems; currently developing NeuroQuit (see Projects).

experience.org: International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (IOAI) — Astana, Kazakhstan
points: Represented Azerbaijan's National Team after earning a Gold Medal at the National Round; selected as 1 of 4 students nationwide to advance to the international round.

Competed at the third IOAI (2–8 Aug 2026), which brought together 466 students from 108 countries and territories, making it the second-largest international science olympiad after the IMO and one centered on hands-on AI problem solving.

experience.org: Leva Mathematical Camp (LMK) — Leva Science Community, Türkiye (Remote)
points: Admitted to a virtual mathematics camp run by a nonprofit science community after a three-stage selection process; an online cultural and academic exchange with participants from middle school through university level across multiple countries.
Work on olympiad-style problems and develop mathematical thinking through peer learning with fellow participants.

experience.org: NASA Space Apps Challenge — Mingachevir, Azerbaijan
points: Lead the Mingachevir Local Event of the NASA International Space Apps Challenge, an annual global hackathon (480,000+ participants across 190+ countries since 2012) where teams use NASA's open data to tackle real challenges on Earth and in space.

Direct the local chapter's two-day hackathon, coordinating outreach, mentorship, and judging with NASA's Global Organizing Team to connect Azerbaijani innovators with NASA's open data and Space Agency Partners.
Co-founded and administer a nonprofit technology community offering free webinars, seminars, and problem-solving discussions to tech enthusiasts of all ages.
Run free, open-to-all competitions with prizes for community members, with the goal of making technology learning accessible regardless of age or background.

Evaluated mobile application submissions in Technovation Girls, the world's largest technology-entrepreneurship competition for girls (370,000+ participants across 120+ countries), giving teams scores and feedback in support of its mission to close the gender gap in technology.
Earned Technovation's Gold Certificate for excellence in evaluation and mentorship.

experience.org: International Youth Math Challenge (IYMC) — Baku, Azerbaijan
points: Represent IYMC (founded 2018; 30,000+ students from 140+ countries) in Azerbaijan. Every participant solves the same problems from the first round, giving students worldwide a fair international stage.
Spearheaded local promotion and organized peer study groups, guiding participants through the Qualification and Pre-Final rounds.
